gaps.note: Cut to panel, possible omitted discussion before Daymond speaks.

stage_a.note: Highly enthusiastic and smiling throughout the presentation and dance demonstration.
Conveys very strong excitement and passion about his inclusive fitness program.
Very friendly, approachable, and considerate, actively inviting the panel to participate.

venture.description: A dance fitness program offering instructor certification and consumer workout DVDs.
venture.note: The founders are asking for an investment to expand the instructor certification side of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 delivers the prepared presentation, explaining his background and demonstrating the inclusive fitness dance program with his team.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokes about losing weight after participating in the dance demonstration.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 compliments the high energy and fun of the demonstration.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks the investors for their positive feedback on the demonstration.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the requested funds are for launching the product, noting the high costs involved.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies the funds are for expanding his instructor certification program, noting his consumer DVDs are already in stores.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks for clarification on whether the consumer products and the certification program are two separate businesses.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms they are separate, explaining that consumer demand led him to create the certification to train more instructors.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks F1 to explain the business model for the certification program.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that instructors pay a fee for a two-day course to become certified for one year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how F1 plans to scale the certification business broadly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they select master trainers in each city to continue hosting certifications after they leave.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for the current combined revenue of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states he does not know the revenue yet because the DVDs were just recently released.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 points out that F1 is asking for investment in the certification business without offering equity in the retail side.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 agrees with S1, stating that F1 is the brand and the two businesses must be combined.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if F1 is willing to combine the two businesses for the investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees to combine them, stating he wants a partner who believes in him and isn't trying to keep everything.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks F1 to share more information about his father's Tae Bo business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that his father created Tae Bo, describing it as the highest-selling fitness DVD in history.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if his father invested in the business, suggesting he should be a strong believer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that his family structure is different and implies his father does not share his wealth with him.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 jokes that his father is a cheapskate.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 laughs at S3's comment about his father.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 suggests that his father might be making him earn his success independently.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees that his father is making him earn it.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how F1 has managed to build the business without his father's financial backing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 credits his wife's support and reveals that they were homeless while building the workout program.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks for confirmation that F1 and his wife were homeless.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that they were indeed homeless.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if his father knew they were homeless and questions how close F1 is to his father.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits they are not close, but notes that their relationship has recently started to improve.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if F1 has the legal rights to use the Billy Blanks Jr name for his business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms there are no issues, noting they share the same agent and his father is aware of his contracts.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 decides to exit, respecting his independence but stating the business model is not clear enough for her.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 decides to exit, expressing respect for his story but not seeing himself as a valuable business partner.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 decides to exit, admiring his perseverance but stating the business is not a suitable investment for him.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 highlights his strategic relationship with Zumba and suggests it could be a valuable asset for F1's program.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 offers one hundred thousand dollars for fifty percent, contingent on Mark joining and Zumba agreeing to distribute the program.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 agrees to join S2's contingent offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 expresses concern about bundling his workout with Zumba, emphasizing his desire to build his own distinct brand.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 explains the deal is a way to accelerate his brand quickly, taking fifty percent of whatever they sell to Zumba.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks F1 why he is concerned, given the potential to reach millions of people through Zumba.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he wants to build his own brand independently rather than being an extension of another workout.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 acknowledges F1's hesitation and attempts to address his concerns about the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks to briefly consult with his wife about the offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 agrees to let him speak with his wife, noting he was about to exit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the offer to his wife in the hallway, noting the Zumba contingency and the fifty percent equity stake.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 expresses difficulty with the offer, emphasizing that F1 himself is the core brand.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks S2 why Zumba wouldn't simply create their own dance program instead of partnering with F1.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 explains that while Zumba could create their own, they lack F1's specific brand value and identity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks F1 if he is ready to accept their offer upon his return.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters, offering to bundle all his businesses for fifty percent but refusing the Zumba contingency to protect his brand.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 insists that F1 is the brand and argues he is misunderstanding the value of the distribution opportunity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 maintains that partnering with Zumba would primarily build Zumba's brand rather than his own.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 disagrees, asking F1 to trust them to accelerate his brand, and pushes for a final yes or no.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 reiterates his desire to eventually be in the dominant market position that Zumba currently holds.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 advises F1 to view Zumba simply as a delivery mechanism for his brand and asks if he will accept.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms he would love to partner with the two investors, but remains hesitant about the contingency.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks F1 for his final decision on the offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 decides to reject the offer, stating he does not believe it is the right deal for his brand.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks the panel for their time and wishes them luck before leaving the tank.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses surprise, feeling that F1 did not fully understand the value of the proposed deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 calls F1's decision a mistake and expresses a strong personal desire to help him succeed.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokes that he will send the founders an invoice for his time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 decides he will regret letting F1 walk away and leaves the tank to follow him.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 speaks with the founders in the hallway, passionately explaining the distribution value of the deal and urging them to reconsider.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts the offer, deeply moved by S2's personal effort to explain the opportunity and help them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 thanks the founders, promising to do everything he can to help them succeed, and they embrace.

decisions.note: Respects his independence but the business model is not clear to her.
Respects his story but does not see himself as a value business partner.
Admires his perseverance but it is not a suitable investment for him.
Contingent on Mark Cuban joining and Zumba agreeing to distribute the program.
Agrees to join Daymond's contingent offer.

decisions.terms: bundle in all my stuff. At the 50%
decisions.note: Offers to bundle both businesses for 50% but without the Zumba contingency.

decisions.terms: I don't think it's the right deal to do
decisions.note: Rejects the offer because he does not want to build someone else's brand.

decisions.terms: if I don't do this, I'm going to regret it
decisions.note: Realizes it's a mistake to let Billy walk away and goes after him.

decisions.terms: I would definitely take that deal
decisions.note: Accepts the original offer after Daymond explains the distribution value in the hall.

record.notes: The founders leave the tank to discuss, and Daymond later leaves the tank to convince them in the hallway.
